Subject: Re: Acceptance escape-hatch for promptset rollout (A/B plan)

Putting a first pass together. High-level suggested gates:

1) Behavioral guardrails (categorical):
- No increase in "unsafe" classification rate > 0.2 percentage points over baseline for top-10 critical intents.
- No new hallucination pattern class appearing > 0.5% of sampled responses.

2) Quantitative score deltas (backwards-compatible metrics):
- NLU intent accuracy drop <= 1.0% absolute
- Rouge-like summary similarity drop <= 1.5% absolute on our golden set
- API error rate (5xx) <= baseline + 0.3%

3) User-impact proxies (customer-facing):
- Median latency increase <= 25ms on the canary path
- Refund/appeal proxy events <= 0.1% of requests in 72h window

If any single high-severity behavioral guardrail trips, auto-fail the canary. For numerical deltas we use the threshold above as primary; small violations (within 0.2-0.5x) will trigger a "hold and investigate" state with a 1-hour pause, >1x triggers immediate rollback.

I will upload the validation scripts and sample evaluation harness to the Drive link. Marissa — can you prioritize surfacing 10 representative prompts from Marco's logs that triggered hallucinations?

—Jonas
Lead, Evals & Quality

Thanks all — quick ops notes and the rollback runbook sketch:

Rollback / escape-hatch (summary):
- Trigger: any single high-severity behavioral guardrail trip OR numerical breach > 1x the threshold.
- Immediate steps (0–15m):
  1) Alert to on-call (Ops) and Evals channel; tag on-call SRE and Evals lead.
  2) Pause canary traffic at the load-balancer routing layer (route new sessions to control model).
  3) Deploy an automated response header marking affected requests for downstream auditing.
- Containment (15–60m):
  1) Roll forward a conservative fallback model variant (we have cached q2-small) or switch to deterministic template for affected intent classes.
  2) Start ingestion of flagged requests into the private incident bucket for root-cause analysis.
- Communication (30–90m):
  1) Notify customer contact with a templated incident note and expected timeline.
  2) If SLA credit is needed, Laura to authorize a temporary credit per playbook.

Operational notes: the latency impact of Marissa's suggested sourcing check is expected to be +40–70ms median; still within the 25–75ms tolerance if we only enable for numeric intents. We can gate by intent to reduce cost.

I'll formalize the runbook as a one-pager and drop into Drive. For now, please confirm owners for on-call contact and draft customer message.

—Kimberly
Director, Runtime & Ops
